did_you_know.text: In ancient Egypt, embalming was meant to preserve the body for the afterlife and was carried out by specialists. That is why Joseph turned to Egypt’s physicians.
The presence of Pharaoh’s officials and Egypt’s elders in the funeral procession shows the great respect they had for Joseph and his family.
In ancient Egypt, chariots and horsemen symbolized military power and high status. Here, they may also have served as an honored escort for the procession.
The name “Abel-mizraim” is a wordplay: “abel” means mourning, recalling Egypt’s great mourning for Jacob.
Mamre is generally identified with the area around Hebron. In the Torah, the Cave of Machpelah became the burial place of the patriarchs and matriarchs.
The biblical phrase “bear the guilt” means to forgive or overlook an offense. The repeated word “please” emphasizes the brothers’ plea.
The question “Am I in God’s place?” is rhetorical: Joseph says that he does not see himself as the ultimate judge of his brothers.
Joseph’s words do not mean that his brothers’ evil act was justified. They express his belief that God can turn even a crisis toward a beneficial outcome.
The verb “I will sustain you” is related to the Hebrew word “כלכלה,” meaning to provide food, care, and support.
